   - valheim-mod
   - rust-oxide-plugin (or rust-oxide, oxide-plugin)
   - minecraft-plugin
   - ark-mod
   - garrysmod (or gmod-addon)
   - csgo-plugin and cs2-plugin (or counterstrikesharp-plugin)
   - 7dtd-mod (or 7-days-to-die)
   - terraria-mod (or tmodloader-mod)
   - spacengineers-mod (or space-engineers-mod)
   - barotrauma-mod

2. Test `GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/license` on 2-3 real repos you found above (one with a clear LICENSE file, and try to find one without) — confirm what it returns: does it give a real SPDX id when a LICENSE exists? What happens when there's no LICENSE file (404? null license field?)? Report exact JSON shape observed.

3. Search for curated "awesome-<game>-modding" style lists on GitHub for Nxeon's game families (Garry's Mod, CS2, Rust/Oxide, Valheim, Minecraft, ARK, 7 Days to Die, Terraria, Space Engineers, Barotrauma, Project Zomboid, etc). Use WebSearch for things like "awesome-garrysmod github", "awesome oxide rust github", "awesome valheim modding github", "awesome cs2 plugins github". Report real repo URLs you find that are actually curated lists (not just guesses) and what's in them.

4. Confirm GitHub's Terms of Service position on using the public search/repo APIs to build a catalog of public repos. Fetch https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service and/or https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api and cite the actual relevant clauses (rate limiting policy, terms about API usage, terms about scraping vs API use).

5. CS2 specifically: research the Metamod:Source + CounterStrikeSharp ecosystem on GitHub. Find:
   - The real Metamod:Source repo (github.com/alliedmodders/metamod-source or similar) and CounterStrikeSharp repo (likely github.com/roflmuffin/CounterStrikeSharp)

Write your findings organized by the 5 numbered items above, with every factual claim cited to a real URL. Flag anything uncertain. Keep it information-dense — this feeds into a larger report, don't pad with fluff. Aim for a thorough but efficient response (you have real API rate limits, don't waste them on redundant calls).
